questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to do an exchange abroad because I wanted to live in another country and meet new people. I chose Edinburgh because I had heard it was a very student friendly city, and because I thought it had a great mix of nature, culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The university provides a good introduction for when you arrive.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university created a little online assignment where they give you a lot of information. You have to read and complete the assignment in order to be fully matriculated. The university also gives you a personal tutor. You meet with them in the first weeks and they can answer any questions you may have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay, but I would recommend starting early to avoid any unnecessary stress. I found my housing via Spareroom, which I would recommend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Again, start searching early as it can take a bit of time to find something.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university won't guarantee housing for Erasmus students studying for one semester, so you have to be aware of that when you apply.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you apply you have to wish for the courses you want. They're not final so you can change later if you're not satisfied.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange team were there via email if you had any questions and were good at answering more general enquiries.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. I wanted some courses for year 2 or 3, however these are often in high demand, so I ended up with some introductory courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be hesitant in changing your courses if you're not satisfied.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were still online and we experienced strikes in the middle of the semester which affected the courses for the worse.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lectures and tutorials are only an hour long, so I would say that you engage with the subjects in a more shallow way than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is a mixture of lectures and tutorials. In tutorials you are 10-15 people. Often tutorials is one big group discussion about a specific reading. I think this differs from UCPH where you often work and discuss in smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Empires (SCAN08010)
- Sociology 1B: The Sociological Imagination: Private Troubles, Public Problems (SCIL08005)
- Language and Communication in Health and Society (SHSS08005)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the course Language and Communication. The course is a part of a social work degree. Therefore, it has both theoretical and practical elements. In the first part of the course we looked at different theories to analyze health communication such as discourse analysis. The second part of the course we practiced how to be a good and empathetic listener in a client-professional setting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most museums and galleries in Scotland are free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university has a lot of different student societies that you can join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really loved the hiking society. They do weekend trips as well, so it was a really great way to see other parts of Scotland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really loved Aisle of Arran. It is a little island close to Glasgow.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was mostly with the other international students. However, I think the easiest way is to join one of the societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any I found particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open and friendly. I'd also recommend going to one of the Cèilidh dances.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join the whatsapp groups. I found most of my friends this way.

2. Start looking for an accommodation early to avoid unnecessary stress.

3. Use your weekends to travel and see Scotland - it's so lovely!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many lovely people and making memories with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Remaining motivated to do the academic work while receiving lectures online and dealing with strikes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
